proof_nl: Assume the hypothesis: g is nonincreasing on [a,b), meaning that for all real x,y with a <= x <= y < b, one has g(y) <= g(x). Now let x,y be any real numbers satisfying a <= x <= y < b. Applying the hypothesis directly to this pair (x,y), we obtain g(y) <= g(x). This is exactly the conclusion. Therefore the statement holds.
solver_summary: The conclusion is a direct restatement of the hypothesis, so the implication follows immediately by unpacking the definition of nonincreasing on [a,b).
